claim: RAUC's efi bootloader backend marks a newly installed slot primary by setting the one-shot EFI BootNext variable (efi-use-bootnext defaults to true); mark-good prepends the slot to BootOrder, mark-bad removes it from BootOrder, and a slot counts as good only while it is listed in BootOrder.

RAUC determines the booted slot from an explicit rauc.slot=<bootname> on the kernel command line before other methods, so a UKI whose signed command line carries rauc.slot= identifies its slot even when booted from a fallback loader path.

EDK II's boot manager (edk2-stable202502, the base of Debian 13's OVMF 2025.02) deletes the BootNext variable before transferring control to that boot option and then walks BootOrder, so a BootNext target that fails to load or start is tried only once per power-on.

systemd-stub (systemd 257): if UEFI Secure Boot is enabled and the UKI has a .cmdline section, any kernel command line passed as invocation parameters (e.g. in an EFI boot entry) is ignored, so the signed command line cannot be overridden from an unauthenticated Boot#### variable.

systemd-stub passes a UKI's .pcrsig and .pcrpkey sections to the kernel as /.extra/tpm2-pcr-signature.json and /.extra/tpm2-pcr-public-key.pem inside the initrd; a non-systemd initrd (Debian initramfs-tools) does not carry these into the booted system, so the signature must be provided another way.

claim: PCR 7 (secure-boot-policy) records the Secure Boot state and changes when Secure Boot is enabled/disabled or the firmware certificates (PK, KEK, db, dbx) change; systemd-cryptenroll binds to PCR 7 only by default.

systemd-cryptenroll --tpm2-public-key= / --tpm2-public-key-pcrs= / --tpm2-signature= binds a LUKS2 key to a signed PCR policy, so any PCR values signed by the key holder unlock it (survives kernel updates) instead of one fixed set of PCR values.

systemd-pcrphase extends PCR 11 with boot-phase strings (enter-initrd, leave-initrd, sysinit, ready, …); enter-initrd/leave-initrd are measured by systemd-pcrphase-initrd.service, which only runs in a systemd-based initrd.

ukify (systemd 257) builds a UKI from a stub, kernel, initrd and command line, signs it for Secure Boot with sbsign, and with --pcr-private-key/--phases calls systemd-measure to embed a signed PCR 11 policy (.pcrsig); systemd-measure needs the TPM2 TSS libraries at build time.

claim: Debian 13 provides every component of this route from its own archive: ovmf 2025.02-8+deb13u1 (OVMF_CODE_4M.secboot.fd), systemd-ukify / systemd-boot-efi 257.13-1~deb13u1, sbsigntool 0.9.4-3.2+deb13u1, efitools 1.9.2-3.5, python3-virt-firmware 24.11-2, swtpm 0.7.1-1.5, rauc 1.13-3+deb13u1, linux-image 6.12.116.

Lab T0: UKIs built with ukify and signed with sbsign by a lab db key pass `sbverify --cert db.crt`; a UKI with one command-line byte changed after signing (panic=5 -> panic=6) and a never-signed UKI both fail it; all four RAUC bundles carry a valid RAUC signature, so firmware refusal is tested independently of RAUC's own bundle check.

Lab T1 (2 runs): on QEMU q35 + OVMF secboot (SMM) with only lab PK/KEK/db enrolled, the 01 §4.3 layout booted a signed UKI with Secure Boot enforced (SecureBoot=1, SetupMode=0, kernel 'Secure boot enabled', lockdown=integrity); a first-boot service created LUKS2 on onemind-data, enrolled a TPM2 (PCR 7) token and a recovery key, wiped the temporary key slot and unlocked it via the TPM with no prompt.

Lab T2 (2 runs): with Debian's unpatched RAUC 1.13 `efi` backend, installing a bundle set BootNext to OneMind-B; slot B booted under Secure Boot, the TPM unlocked the data without a prompt, the health gate committed B (BootOrder starts with OneMind-B) and a second reboot stayed on B. No GRUB, shim or systemd-boot was used.

Lab T3 (2 runs): a signed but unhealthy update (v3) booted under Secure Boot, its data unlocked by the TPM, the gate ran mark-bad (RAUC removed OneMind-A from BootOrder) and rebooted; the box came back on B (v2) with data unlocked and no human input, within 2 boots.

Lab T4/T5 (2 runs each): OVMF refused a UKI tampered after signing and an unsigned UKI with 'BdsDxe: failed to load Boot0003 "OneMind-A" … : Access Denied'; because RAUC had only set the one-shot BootNext, the same power-on continued down BootOrder to the committed slot B, with data unlocked and no human input.

Lab T6 (2 runs): the same disk and TPM booted with Secure Boot disabled (SecureBootEnable=false, same keys) ran slot B, but the PCR 7-bound TPM2 unseal was refused ('Password querying disabled via headless option'), /data stayed locked, no prompt blocked boot and the gate did not commit; re-enabling Secure Boot unlocked the data again (T6b).

Lab T7 bonus (2 runs): a LUKS2 container bound only to a signed PCR 11 policy (+PCR 7), with the policy signed at UKI build time by a lab key, unlocked on slot A, on slot B, on the unhealthy v3 slot and after rollback. With Debian's initramfs-tools initrd the stub's /.extra signature file is not carried over, so the lab shipped each UKI's .pcrsig in the root filesystem; phases measured were 'sysinit' and 'ready' only.

Lab E1 (exploratory, not pre-registered, 1 run): with BootNext pointed at the firmware's auto-created disk entry (simulating both OneMind entries failing), OVMF booted the ESP's factory loader, an OLD but validly signed UKI (v1), under Secure Boot against slot A's newer v5 root filesystem; the PCR 7-only data key unlocked and the health gate committed slot A as good. Secure Boot plus PCR 7 does not stop a downgrade to any older signed kernel; only the signed-PCR-11 container refused.

Lab: RAUC's efi backend reports a never-written slot as 'boot status: good' merely because its entry is in BootOrder; during install RAUC removes the target from BootOrder (BootOrder became '0003' only); OVMF re-adds its own auto-created entries (UiApp, the disk removable-media paths) to BootOrder on the following boot.

Lab: the 01 §4.3 layout (1 GiB ESP, 512 MiB FAT32 ESP-type boot-a/b, 10 GiB system-a/b with a 1.6 GiB root image, 1 GiB recovery, LUKS2 data) needed no change for the signed-UKI route: each boot slot took a 200 MiB vfat image holding both per-slot UKIs; whole suite T1–T7 took 781 s and 818 s under x86_64 TCG emulation on the M5 Mac (first boot 74–75 s).
